Samantha —

Thanks for the detail and the CSV. We can absolutely model a two-quarter smoothing for the uplift portion; the main constraint is how to treat true-up/usage overage if you exceed the blended commit during Q1. I sketched two options below:

Option A — Smoothing (preferred for procurement)
- Apply 50% of agreed uplift in Q1 invoice and 50% in Q2 (invoice schedule unchanged)
- Unit price for smoothed portion is the blended uplift rate; overall blended impact to average unit price is +6.2% vs current run-rate
- True-up: any usage above committed bucket billed at standard overage rate monthly (no retroactive recalculation)

Option B — Deferred recognition (preferred for finance)
- Defer 40% of uplift to a credit schedule (applies as invoice credit in Q2)
- Keeps Q1 spend lower but requires a credit memo in Q2 and legal sign-off on amendment

If we go with Option A we can also co-term to Jan 1 by pro-rating the remaining months so the commit resets on that date. I'll loop Ben and Marissa to nail the commercial.
